newsitem.title: USA: CFTC puts CME cheese contract on fast track.
newsitem.headline: CFTC puts CME cheese contract on fast track.

text.p: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission said Friday it would accept comments until August 4 on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange's plan to trade futures and options on cheddar cheese.

In a Federal Register notice, the CFTC said it would use "fast-track" procedures to review the contract application. That means the contracts could be approved by the agency as early as August 25, or 45 days after the application.
The fast-track review also means that public comment on the proposal will last 15 days, rather than the typical 30-day period.

The Chicago Mercantile Exchange's board of directors earlier this month said it wanted to add cheddar cheese futures for trading in increments of 40-pound blocks. The market will be based on the cash settlement using a weekly price issued by the Agriculture Department's National Agricultural Statistics Service.
A wholesale cheese market moved to the CME on May 1 after 41 years at the National Cheese Exchange in Green Bay.
